claims.text: Fine-grained, twin-prone CoCrFeMnNi forms deformation twins during high-strain-rate loading.
Dynamic twin formation activates additional slip systems.
Dynamic twinning enhances strength while preserving ductility relative to coarse-grained, twin-poor CoCrFeMnNi.
The investigated CoCrFeMnNi alloy is single-phase FCC.
Severe plastic deformation followed by controlled annealing can produce a fine-grained, twin-rich CoCrFeMnNi condition.
Processing can produce a coarse-grained, twin-poor CoCrFeMnNi baseline.
High strain rates and cryogenic temperatures promote deformation twinning in CoCrFeMnNi.
Twin-induced barriers raise yield strength by obstructing dislocation motion.
Deformation twinning produces dynamic strain partitioning.
Dynamic strain partitioning enhances ductility by making plastic deformation more uniform.
The fine-grained, twin-rich alloy will have a higher work-hardening rate than the coarse-grained, twin-poor baseline under dynamic loading.
The fine-grained, twin-rich alloy will have higher yield strength than the coarse-grained, twin-poor baseline under dynamic loading.
The fine-grained, twin-rich alloy will have greater ductility than the coarse-grained, twin-poor baseline under dynamic loading.
Under high strain rates and low temperatures, greater deformation-twin density will correlate with superior strength and ductility.
The proposed effect should hold from cryogenic to room temperature and at strain rates up to approximately 10^3 s^-1.
The twinning effect may diminish at higher temperatures because twinning is less favored.
The twinning effect may diminish at extreme strain rates when other deformation mechanisms dominate.
Differences in dislocation density and residual stress may also affect the observed mechanical response.
